exposure: Type of fetal head molding (occipitoparietal, frontoparietal, parietoparietal)
outcome: Presence and type of fetal head molding (ultrasound-assessed)
Delivery mode (spontaneous vaginal, vacuum extraction, failed vacuum extraction)
cohort: The study included 144 nulliparous women with a single fetus in cephalic presentation who experienced slow progress in the active second stage of labor.
finding: Fetal head molding was observed in 55% of fetuses, with occipitoparietal molding being common in occiput anterior positions, and different types of molding can be classified with ultrasound.
mod_finding: Occipitoparietal molding was not significantly associated with delivery mode, whereas frontoparietal and parietoparietal moldings were less frequent and rarely resulted in spontaneous delivery.
cross-section timing: During the active second stage of labor with pushing, when an operative intervention was considered.
